A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite appendix additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, formulation-residual measurements, camera-distortion evaluations, and extensive ablation and noise-robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds DiLiGenT-MV evaluations and experiments with a new outlier-filtering strategy.

M1.justification: Appendix H adds a concrete outlier filter: detect extreme omega coefficients, sample alternative interpolation parameters, and select the coefficient closest to one. This extends the earlier normal-averaging strategies and adaptive-ray discussion into a new procedure; the central formulation and optimization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds DiLiGenT-MV, covering 20 viewpoints of five objects with ground-truth and photometric-stereo normals. This broadens viewpoint coverage within the existing object-reconstruction domain; real photometric-stereo inputs and the underlying normal-integration task were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: BiNI and Kim et al. remain the comparison methods. The new DiLiGenT-MV experiment extends the existing BiNI comparison, while the newly cited integration papers are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The added DiLiGenT-MV protocol averages absolute depth error over 20 views per object, uses BlenderProc-rendered reference depths, and applies outlier filtering with epsilon_out = 0.1. The added noise-filter experiments use 0.01. Existing experimental settings are retained, including the 1200-iteration budget.

E4.justification: Figures 12 and 13 extend the existing outlier and rotational-noise analyses with an adaptive-ray filtering variant, testing whether it removes spikes beyond normal averaging. The tested object, perturbation levels, earlier variants, and other ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The existing means and standard deviations across pixels remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 9 averages different viewpoints rather than repeated stochastic runs.

E6.justification: Table 9 substantially extends the evidence with quantitative results for ground-truth and photometric-stereo normals across multiple viewpoints, beyond v1's qualitative real-input demonstrations. For example, buddha photometric-stereo error is 1.02 mm for Ours versus 1.14 for BiNI. New filtering results also appear in Figures 12–13. Tables 1–8 and earlier noise-result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds an alternative derivation using direct normal–point dot-product constraints, Eqs. 21–25, alongside the original coordinate-based derivation. The existing formulation, propositions, and positivity proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: more accurate depth–normal modeling, state-of-the-art benchmark performance, explicit discontinuity handling, and direct applicability to generic central cameras.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds a mechanism explanation linking near-zero normal–ray dot products to extreme coefficients and spike artifacts. The limitations discussion changes from further noise mitigation as future work to an explicit requirement for physically meaningful normals and preprocessing. Appendix I additionally interprets the new results as supporting photometric-stereo applicability.

D1.justification: v2 documents the outlier-detection threshold, interpolation search interval, coefficient-selection rule, and experiment-specific epsilon_out values. It also describes rendering DiLiGenT-MV reference depths from meshes and camera parameters. Hardware, timing information, and code-access disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Cao et al.'s inverse-plane-fitting method, Heep and Zell's adaptive meshing method, and Li et al.'s multi-view photometric-stereo benchmark. These support the new artifact discussion and evaluation; the main related-work positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The main text receives small grammatical edits, a shortened concluding phrase, and acknowledgements. The supplement adds an alternative derivation, an outlier-filtering subsection, and an evaluation appendix; limitations move from Appendix I to J. There is no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9 and expands Figures 12–13 with another reconstruction/error block, resizing and redisplaying existing panels. Several appendix tables and figures shift position, and Figure 5's caption clarifies the error-map viewpoint. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's qualitative real-input evidence with quantitative DiLiGenT-MV comparisons and extends averaging-based noise mitigation with an explicit, tested filter. The alternative derivation also makes the formulation easier to verify. These are useful targeted gains, although robustness demonstrations remain limited and improvements are not uniform: Table 9's reading photometric-stereo error increases from 1.14 to 1.24 mm when discontinuity estimation is enabled.
